Jenny decided to enter numbers into the cells of a 3 \times 3 table so that the sum of the numbers in all four possible 2 \times 2 cells will be the same. The numbers in three of the corner cells have already been written, as shown.
Which number should she write in the fourth corner cell?

method.method_draft: Read the 3×3 grid from the image as having corner entries top-left 2, top-right 4, bottom-right 3, and bottom-left unknown x. From the text, use the condition that all four 2×2 subtable sums are equal. Label the grid entries as a,b,c / d,e,f / x,h,3 with a=2 and c=4. Compare the two upper 2×2 sums: 2+b+d+e = b+4+e+f, so d-f=2. Compare the two lower 2×2 sums: d+e+x+h = e+f+h+3, so d-f=3-x. Equate these two expressions for d-f to get 2=3-x, hence x=1.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a 3×3 grid with corners 2, 4, 3, and unknown x in the lower-left corner. From the text, all four 2×2 block sums are equal. Label the top-middle cell p and bottom-middle cell q.
